# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids

  deployments when the spec is `dial`, else OpenAI `/models`; the saved
  entry's own key authenticates; failures fall back to manual entry).

  `ModelRolesResolver.setRoleChain`/`clearRoleChain` (the resolver is
  created on demand when the config had no `roles:` section —
  `AgentCliConfig.modelRolesResolver` is mutable) and persists via
  `onModelsConfigChanged` (bin/fah.dart's persistConfig reads the live
  resolver config).

  YAML (`.fah/cubes/<name>.yaml`, apiVersion fa/v1 kind Cube) with
  tool/network/fs/env/resource/cache policies (deny-wins, empty allowlist =
  deny-all, lexical path normalization as traversal guard), `CubeResolver`
  (path > name lookup), Dart-layer enforcement (`SandboxedExecutionEnv`
  decorator: `CubeFsGuard` gates the agent's own read/edit/write tools,
  `CubePolicyEngine` gates bash incl. pipes/`$(...)` subshells and shell
  redirect targets (`>`/`>>`/`<>`/`&>`/`2>` writes, `<` reads, `2>&1`
  exempt; arguments stay name-gated only), exit 127
  denials with per-exec reason), content-addressed `CubeCacheManager` under
  `.fah/cube-cache/<md5>/` (manifest + ttl). `spec.backend:` = `policy`
  (default, Dart-only) | `kernel` opt-in: every command wrapped in the OS
  sandbox via `CubeSandboxBackend.wrapCommand` — macOS `sandbox-exec -f
  <profile>`, Linux `unshare --user --map-root-user --mount [--net iff the
  spec allows no network]` + `ulimit -v/-t` ceilings, both over a clean
  `env -i` environment; profiles staged content-verified under
  `<home>/.fah/cube-profiles/<md5>.sb` (outside the guest-writable
  workspace; re-verified against the recomputed profile before every
  wrapped exec — #790); kernel mode fail-closes (`fa_cube[<name>]:`
  error, no exec) when the staging location is not provably
  guest-unwritable — a `homeDir` inside/relative-to the workspace or a
  spec mount granting rw over it (the refusal names
  `spec.allowDegrade: true` as the explicit policy-mode escape hatch;
  with it set, the bind degrades and `onDegrade` fires); the staging
  dir is swept once per
  binding for this profile's own `.tmp` orphans (other bindings' files
  untouched); the macOS SBPL profile denies writes blanket outside the
  workspace + `rw` mounts (`/dev/null`, `/dev/fd` exempt) and denies reads
  of `/etc` + user homes when no root mount grants reads (a blanket read
  deny would abort exec — dyld); Windows = Job Object descriptor only
  (kernel on a platform without an enforcing backend is REFUSED — clean
  `fa_cube[<name>]:` error naming `spec.allowDegrade`, zero commands —
  unless the spec opts in via `allowDegrade: true`, which degrades to
  policy mode with the loud `fa_cube[<name>]: kernel backend unavailable,

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1384
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1384
- **Title**: feat(1377): auto_update tri-state flag — notify banner, autonomous verified self-update, /update
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1377-config-flag-self-update` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1599
- **Deletions**: -47
- **Created**: 2026-10-07T13:20:08Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-07T13:32:10Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1377

## Scope map — delivered vs the issue

| Issue AC | Delivered |
|---|---|
| `auto_update: false` → zero update network | boot hook arm returns before any fetch; the flag never reaches the updater |
| `auto_update: notify` (default) → one-line non-blocking banner, once per session | bounded (~3 s) `fetchLatestTag` at boot, `fa vX available → run: fa update` on the pre-TUI boot-notice channel (stderr), once-per-process guard |
| `auto_update: true` → download, verify, apply, restart transparently | `applyUpdate` before session boot: fetch → **provenance-verified** download → atomic swap → spawn successor with the ORIGINAL argv (inherited stdio) → exit(0); successor resumes the session through its own `--session` flag |
| failed update never crashes or interrupts | every failure is an `ApplyUpdateOutcome`; boot continues on the current binary; one warn, never a throw path |
| update events logged to `~/.fah/logs/fa.log` | `logUpdateLine`: `fa update applied: vX -> vY` (same file/format as the CLI diagnostic log); restart failures logged too |
| `/settings` exposes auto_update and persists it | settings-hub row cycles `notify → true → false`, validates with the real parser, persists to the **global** file; cycling back to `notify` drops the key (defaults never written) |
| `/update` on latest | `already up to date (v…)` — no restart |
| `/update` with newer | settles the active run, drains queued composer drafts to completion, applies, restarts **in the same terminal** (spawn successor + inherited stdio + original argv), session resumes with full history |
| Windows graceful prompt-restart fallback | swap completes, prints `updated to vX — restart fa to use it.`, no self-restart (documented) |

Issue-scope notes: the notify check runs at startup only (the issue offers "or periodically in background" — startup-only is the delivered scope); serve/wire-daemon boots are excluded from the hook (a daemon must not restart itself under connected clients).

## Security design (trust boundaries)

- **Trust anchor**: `kFaReleaseSigningPem` — byte-identical to `TRUSTED_SIGNING_PEM` in `site/install.sh` (machine-checked diff). The updater trusts the SAME pinned key the installer trusts; a release without signed provenance cannot install.
- **Verification before any swap** (`verifyReleaseProvenance`): downloads the release's `SHA256SUMS` + `SHA256SUMS.sig`, verifies the RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 SHA-256 signature with `package:cryptography` (`RsaSsaPkcs1v15`, pure Dart — works on Windows too, no openssl shell-out), DER-parses the pinned SPKI, then compares the archive's sha256 against the signed manifest line. **Any** failure (missing manifest, bad signature, unlisted asset, digest mismatch, tampered byte) → false → nothing installed.
- **Atomic swap + rollback**: extract to temp, one-generation `.bak` of the current binary kept on Unix (Windows keeps its existing `.old`), rename-over; a failed successor spawn leaves the new binary in place with the `.bak` for manual rollback and one honest warning.
- **Restart**: spawn-successor-then-exit (Dart has no exec-replace) — fixed short settle delay as the ready check; a successor that already exited non-zero within the window counts as a failed restart.
- **No telemetry**: one `fa.log` line per event, nothing else.

## Trust-path bug fixed during review

`_manifestDigest` originally parsed the manifest with a single-space regex — real `sha256sum` output is **two spaces**, so every genuine release would have failed verification (fail-closed, but a total functional break). Fixed and regression-pinned: the test fixture manifest uses real two-space format.

## Disclosure (local verification)

The dart VM is SIGKILLed on the shared host (exit 137 on `pub get`, both system and temp SDKs — machine guard active during this lane; attempts: 3, per lane rules no retry loop). **Static verification instead of a local run**:

- PEM trust anchor: byte-identity to `site/install.sh` machine-checked (python diff) — identical.
- DER SPKI parser: exact python mirror of the Dart code over both keys — pinned 4096-bit key extracts n (512 B) / e = [1,0,1] correctly.
- Crypto chain proven offline end-to-end with host openssl: fresh keypair → signed `SHA256SUMS` → `openssl dgst -sha256 -verify` OK, plus an independent python PKCS#1 v1.5 verification using the parser-extracted key — OK.
- Manifest regex validated against real `sha256sum` shapes (two-space, one-space, `*`-marker, trailing whitespace).
- Cross-slice consistency probed mechanically: every enum arm / function / field referenced by the wiring exists where expected; structural balance on all 13 touched files; cryptography 2.9.0 API confirmed against pub-cache source.
- **PR CI is the real gate**: targeted suites `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` (48 tests), `test/cli/boot_update_test.dart`, `test/config/auto_update_test.dart`, plus the parity/help rot-guards are expected green; reviewers should treat red CI here as the bug report.

## Test surface (AC-first)

48 engine tests (compareVersions matrix, 5-platform asset naming, PEM/DER parse, provenance happy/tampered/404/unlisted/wrong-key, applyUpdate outcome matrix with fixture downloader + fake spawn, successor handshake, `.bak` retention, log format), boot-decision matrix, strict parse matrix + service-mirror agreement pin + persistence round-trip (default never written), rot-guards updated for the new slash command and help keywords.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs

1. **`spawnSuccessor`**: `await Future<void>.delayed(settleDelay);` then `process.exitCode.then(...).timeout(Duration.zero, ...)`. Note: `exitCode` future is already completing potentially. OK.

2. **`applyUpdate` catch-all**: catches everything and returns downloadFailed — even a provenance failure would already be returned as such. But the catch is broad — including errors from `_extractAndSwap` (which could happen mid-swap — e.g. after the `.bak` copy but before rename). OK-ish.

3. **`applyUpdate` in `_restartAfterUpdate`**: for pub-global, `spawn` seam applies only for binary; the else branch uses spawnSuccessor which calls `_detectInstall()` again. Fine.

4. **Restart failure leaves new binary in place with `.bak`** — documented.

6. **`_manifestDigest`**: regex `^([0-9a-fA-F]{64})[ \t]+\*?(.+?)[ \t]*$` applied on `line.trim()`. Hmm — `line.trim()` trims the leading whitespace, but sha256sum lines for filenames with leading spaces use ` <name>` (space-prefix indicates leading space in name). Trimming would break those names — but these are controlled asset names, fine.

   The match on `(.+?)` non-greedy with trailing `[ \t]*$` — trailing whitespace in the name is excluded. But what about a name that ends with a space legitimately? Not our assets. OK.

   One subtle issue: `hex.decode(expected)` — if the digest is 64 hex chars, decode yields 32 bytes. OK.

7. **`verifyReleaseProvenance`**: fetches sums and sig in sequence — both non-200 → false. Verifies signature over `sums.bodyBytes`. Then digest compare. Good. But note: **no cross-check that `archiveName` downloaded is the ONLY listed entry** — not needed.

   A subtle issue: the SHA256SUMS fetch and archive download are NOT done over a pinned connection, but HTTPS is used. TOFU-ish but fine.

   Potential issue: `hex.decode(expected)` could throw FormatException if expected is odd — but regex pins to 64 hex chars, so fine.

8. **TOCTOU between verify and swap**: archive bytes are verified in memory and then written from the same bytes — good, no TOCTOU.

9. **`spawnSuccessor`** catches spawn errors. But after `exit(0)` in the caller — with `ProcessStartMode.inheritedStdio`, the parent exits and the child takes over the terminal. OK for design.

10. **Windows `.old` aside**: `File(target).renameSync(aside); File(staging).renameSync(target);` — no cleanup of aside afterwards (documented "Windows keeps its existing .old").

11. **`_extractZip`**: writes entries without path traversal check — a zip-slip concern! `final dest = File('${tmpDir.path}/${parts.join('/')}');` — if an entry name contains `..`, e.g. `../../home/user/.bashrc`, `parts.join('/')` would produce `..` segments. ZipDecoder may normalize? The `archive` package's ZipDecoder does NOT sanitize paths by default (I believe older versions don't; newer have some protections in `decodeBytes`? Actually the `archive` package's `ZipDecoder` doesn't guard against path traversal; extraction via `extractFiles` etc. is manual here anyway).     "summary": "feat(1377): auto_update tri-state flag — notify banner, autonomous verified self-update, /update",
    "description": "Fixes #1377

## Scope map — delivered vs the issue

| Issue AC | Delivered |
|---|---|
| `auto_update: false` → zero update network | boot hook arm returns before any fetch; the flag never reaches the updater |
| `auto_update: notify` (default) → one-line non-blocking banner, once per session | bounded (~3 s) `fetchLatestTag` at boot, `fa vX available → run: fa update` on the pre-TUI boot-notice channel (stderr), once-per-process guard |
| `auto_update: true` → download, verify, apply, restart transparently | `applyUpdate` before session boot: fetch → **provenance-verified** download → atomic swap → spawn successor with the ORIGINAL argv (inherited stdio) → exit(0); successor resumes the session through its own `--session` flag |
| failed update never crashes or interrupts | every failure is an `ApplyUpdateOutcome`; boot continues on the current binary; one warn, never a throw path |
| update events logged to `~/.fah/logs/fa.log` | `logUpdateLine`: `fa update applied: vX -> vY` (same file/format as the CLI diagnostic log); restart failures logged too |
| `/settings` exposes auto_update and persists it | settings-hub row cycles `notify → true → false`, validates with the real parser, persists to the **global** file; cycling back to `notify` drops the key (defaults never written) |
| `/update` on latest | `already up to date (v…)` — no restart |
| `/update` with newer | settles the active run, drains queued composer drafts to completion, applies, restarts **in the same terminal** (spawn successor + inherited stdio + original argv), session resumes with full history |
| Windows graceful prompt-restart fallback | swap completes, prints `updated to vX — restart fa to use it.`, no self-restart (documented) |

Issue-scope notes: the notify check runs at startup only (the issue offers "or periodically in background" — startup-only is the delivered scope); serve/wire-daemon boots are excluded from the hook (a daemon must not restart itself under connected clients).

## Security design (trust boundaries)

- **Trust anchor**: `kFaReleaseSigningPem` — byte-identical to `TRUSTED_SIGNING_PEM` in `site/install.sh` (machine-checked diff). The updater trusts the SAME pinned key the installer trusts; a release without signed provenance cannot install.
- **Verification before any swap** (`verifyReleaseProvenance`): downloads the release's `SHA256SUMS` + `SHA256SUMS.sig`, verifies the RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 SHA-256 signature with `package:cryptography` (`RsaSsaPkcs1v15`, pure Dart — works on Windows too, no openssl shell-out), DER-parses the pinned SPKI, then compares the archive's sha256 against the signed manifest line. **Any** failure (missing manifest, bad signature, unlisted asset, digest mismatch, tampered byte) → false → nothing installed.
- **Atomic swap + rollback**: extract to temp, one-generation `.bak` of the current binary kept on Unix (Windows keeps its existing `.old`), rename-over; a failed successor spawn leaves the new binary in place with the `.bak` for manual rollback and one honest warning.
- **Restart**: spawn-successor-then-exit (Dart has no exec-replace) — fixed short settle delay as the ready check; a successor that already exited non-zero within the window counts as a failed restart.
- **No telemetry**: one `fa.log` line per event, nothing else.

## Trust-path bug fixed during review

`_manifestDigest` originally parsed the manifest with a single-space regex — real `sha256sum` output is **two spaces**, so every genuine release would have failed verification (fail-closed, but a total functional break). Fixed and regression-pinned: the test fixture manifest uses real two-space format.

## Disclosure (local verification)

The dart VM is SIGKILLed on the shared host (exit 137 on `pub get`, both system and temp SDKs — machine guard active during this lane; attempts: 3, per lane rules no retry loop). **Static verification instead of a local run**:

- PEM trust anchor: byte-identity to `site/install.sh` machine-checked (python diff) — identical.
- DER SPKI parser: exact python mirror of the Dart code over both keys — pinned 4096-bit key extracts n (512 B) / e = [1,0,1] correctly.
- Crypto chain proven offline end-to-end with host openssl: fresh keypair → signed `SHA256SUMS` → `openssl dgst -sha256 -verify` OK, plus an independent python PKCS#1 v1.5 verification using the parser-extracted key — OK.
- Manifest regex validated against real `sha256sum` shapes (two-space, one-space, `*`-marker, trailing whitespace).
- Cross-slice consistency probed mechanically: every enum arm / function / field referenced by the wiring exists where expected; structural balance on all 13 touched files; cryptography 2.9.0 API confirmed against pub-cache source.
- **PR CI is the real gate**: targeted suites `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` (48 tests), `test/cli/boot_update_test.dart`, `test/config/auto_update_test.dart`, plus the parity/help rot-guards are expected green; reviewers should treat red CI here as the bug report.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +

- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):

  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids

  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are

  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a

  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable

  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;

  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual

    "description": "Fixes #1377

## Scope map — delivered vs the issue

| Issue AC | Delivered |
|---|---|
| `auto_update: false` → zero update network | boot hook arm returns before any fetch; the flag never reaches the updater |
| `auto_update: notify` (default) → one-line non-blocking banner, once per session | bounded (~3 s) `fetchLatestTag` at boot, `fa vX available → run: fa update` on the pre-TUI boot-notice channel (stderr), once-per-process guard |
| `auto_update: true` → download, verify, apply, restart transparently | `applyUpdate` before session boot: fetch → **provenance-verified** download → atomic swap → spawn successor with the ORIGINAL argv (inherited stdio) → exit(0); successor resumes the session through its own `--session` flag |
| failed update never crashes or interrupts | every failure is an `ApplyUpdateOutcome`; boot continues on the current binary; one warn, never a throw path |
| update events logged to `~/.fah/logs/fa.log` | `logUpdateLine`: `fa update applied: vX -> vY` (same file/format as the CLI diagnostic log); restart failures logged too |
| `/settings` exposes auto_update and persists it | settings-hub row cycles `notify → true → false`, validates with the real parser, persists to the **global** file; cycling back to `notify` drops the key (defaults never written) |
| `/update` on latest | `already up to date (v…)` — no restart |
| `/update` with newer | settles the active run, drains queued composer drafts to completion, applies, restarts **in the same terminal** (spawn successor + inherited stdio + original argv), session resumes with full history |
| Windows graceful prompt-restart fallback | swap completes, prints `updated to vX — restart fa to use it.`, no self-restart (documented) |

Issue-scope notes: the notify check runs at startup only (the issue offers "or periodically in background" — startup-only is the delivered scope); serve/wire-daemon boots are excluded from the hook (a daemon must not restart itself under connected clients).

## Security design (trust boundaries)

- **Trust anchor**: `kFaReleaseSigningPem` — byte-identical to `TRUSTED_SIGNING_PEM` in `site/install.sh` (machine-checked diff). The updater trusts the SAME pinned key the installer trusts; a release without signed provenance cannot install.
- **Verification before any swap** (`verifyReleaseProvenance`): downloads the release's `SHA256SUMS` + `SHA256SUMS.sig`, verifies the RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 SHA-256 signature with `package:cryptography` (`RsaSsaPkcs1v15`, pure Dart — works on Windows too, no openssl shell-out), DER-parses the pinned SPKI, then compares the archive's sha256 against the signed manifest line. **Any** failure (missing manifest, bad signature, unlisted asset, digest mismatch, tampered byte) → false → nothing installed.
- **Atomic swap + rollback**: extract to temp, one-generation `.bak` of the current binary kept on Unix (Windows keeps its existing `.old`), rename-over; a failed successor spawn leaves the new binary in place with the `.bak` for manual rollback and one honest warning.
- **Restart**: spawn-successor-then-exit (Dart has no exec-replace) — fixed short settle delay as the ready check; a successor that already exited non-zero within the window counts as a failed restart.
- **No telemetry**: one `fa.log` line per event, nothing else.

`_manifestDigest` originally parsed the manifest with a single-space regex — real `sha256sum` output is **two spaces**, so every genuine release would have failed verification (fail-closed, but a total functional break). Fixed and regression-pinned: the test fixture manifest uses real two-space format.

The dart VM is SIGKILLed on the shared host (exit 137 on `pub get`, both system and temp SDKs — machine guard active during this lane; attempts: 3, per lane rules no retry loop). **Static verification instead of a local run**:

- Manifest regex validated against real `sha256sum` shapes (two-space, one-space, `*`-marker, trailing whitespace).
- Cross-slice consistency probed mechanically: every enum arm / function / field referenced by the wiring exists where expected; structural balance on all 13 touched files; cryptography 2.9.0 API confirmed against pub-cache source.
- **PR CI is the real gate**: targeted suites `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` (48 tests), `test/cli/boot_update_test.dart`, `test/config/auto_update_test.dart`, plus the parity/help rot-guards are expected green; reviewers should treat red CI here as the bug report.

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe

  "fields": {
    "summary": "feat(1377): auto_update tri-state flag — notify banner, autonomous verified self-update, /update",
    "description": "Fixes #1377

## Scope map — delivered vs the issue

| Issue AC | Delivered |
|---|---|
| `auto_update: false` → zero update network | boot hook arm returns before any fetch; the flag never reaches the updater |
| `auto_update: notify` (default) → one-line non-blocking banner, once per session | bounded (~3 s) `fetchLatestTag` at boot, `fa vX available → run: fa update` on the pre-TUI boot-notice channel (stderr), once-per-process guard |
| `auto_update: true` → download, verify, apply, restart transparently | `applyUpdate` before session boot: fetch → **provenance-verified** download → atomic swap → spawn successor with the ORIGINAL argv (inherited stdio) → exit(0); successor resumes the session through its own `--session` flag |
| failed update never crashes or interrupts | every failure is an `ApplyUpdateOutcome`; boot continues on the current binary; one warn, never a throw path |
| update events logged to `~/.fah/logs/fa.log` | `logUpdateLine`: `fa update applied: vX -> vY` (same file/format as the CLI diagnostic log); restart failures logged too |
| `/settings` exposes auto_update and persists it | settings-hub row cycles `notify → true → false`, validates with the real parser, persists to the **global** file; cycling back to `notify` drops the key (defaults never written) |
| `/update` on latest | `already up to date (v…)` — no restart |
| `/update` with newer | settles the active run, drains queued composer drafts to completion, applies, restarts **in the same terminal** (spawn successor + inherited stdio + original argv), session resumes with full history |
| Windows graceful prompt-restart fallback | swap completes, prints `updated to vX — restart fa to use it.`, no self-restart (documented) |

Issue-scope notes: the notify check runs at startup only (the issue offers "or periodically in background" — startup-only is the delivered scope); serve/wire-daemon boots are excluded from the hook (a daemon must not restart itself under connected clients).

## Security design (trust boundaries)

- **Trust anchor**: `kFaReleaseSigningPem` — byte-identical to `TRUSTED_SIGNING_PEM` in `site/install.sh` (machine-checked diff). The updater trusts the SAME pinned key the installer trusts; a release without signed provenance cannot install.
- **Verification before any swap** (`verifyReleaseProvenance`): downloads the release's `SHA256SUMS` + `SHA256SUMS.sig`, verifies the RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 SHA-256 signature with `package:cryptography` (`RsaSsaPkcs1v15`, pure Dart — works on Windows too, no openssl shell-out), DER-parses the pinned SPKI, then compares the archive's sha256 against the signed manifest line. **Any** failure (missing manifest, bad signature, unlisted asset, digest mismatch, tampered byte) → false → nothing installed.
- **Atomic swap + rollback**: extract to temp, one-generation `.bak` of the current binary kept on Unix (Windows keeps its existing `.old`), rename-over; a failed successor spawn leaves the new binary in place with the `.bak` for manual rollback and one honest warning.
- **Restart**: spawn-successor-then-exit (Dart has no exec-replace) — fixed short settle delay as the ready check; a successor that already exited non-zero within the window counts as a failed restart.
- **No telemetry**: one `fa.log` line per event, nothing else.

## Trust-path bug fixed during review

`_manifestDigest` originally parsed the manifest with a single-space regex — real `sha256sum` output is **two spaces**, so every genuine release would have failed verification (fail-closed, but a total functional break). Fixed and regression-pinned: the test fixture manifest uses real two-space format.

## Disclosure (local verification)

The dart VM is SIGKILLed on the shared host (exit 137 on `pub get`, both system and temp SDKs — machine guard active during this lane; attempts: 3, per lane rules no retry loop). **Static verification instead of a local run**:

- PEM trust anchor: byte-identity to `site/install.sh` machine-checked (python diff) — identical.
- DER SPKI parser: exact python mirror of the Dart code over both keys — pinned 4096-bit key extracts n (512 B) / e = [1,0,1] correctly.
- Crypto chain proven offline end-to-end with host openssl: fresh keypair → signed `SHA256SUMS` → `openssl dgst -sha256 -verify` OK, plus an independent python PKCS#1 v1.5 verification using the parser-extracted key — OK.
- Manifest regex validated against real `sha256sum` shapes (two-space, one-space, `*`-marker, trailing whitespace).
- Cross-slice consistency probed mechanically: every enum arm / function / field referenced by the wiring exists where expected; structural balance on all 13 touched files; cryptography 2.9.0 API confirmed against pub-cache source.
- **PR CI is the real gate**: targeted suites `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` (48 tests), `test/cli/boot_update_test.dart`, `test/config/auto_update_test.dart`, plus the parity/help rot-guards are expected green; reviewers should treat red CI here as the bug report.

## Test surface (AC-first)

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):

  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids

  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a

  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual

  deployments when the spec is `dial`, else OpenAI `/models`; the saved
  entry's own key authenticates; failures fall back to manual entry).
  `startAgentModelFlow` pins the `smol`/`subagent` role chains through
  `ModelRolesResolver.setRoleChain`/`clearRoleChain` (the resolver is
  created on demand when the config had no `roles:` section —

{
  "key": "pr-1384",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "feat(1377): auto_update tri-state flag — notify banner, autonomous verified self-update, /update",
    "description": "Fixes #1377

## Scope map — delivered vs the issue

| Issue AC | Delivered |
|---|---|
| `auto_update: false` → zero update network | boot hook arm returns before any fetch; the flag never reaches the updater |
| `auto_update: notify` (default) → one-line non-blocking banner, once per session | bounded (~3 s) `fetchLatestTag` at boot, `fa vX available → run: fa update` on the pre-TUI boot-notice channel (stderr), once-per-process guard |
| `auto_update: true` → download, verify, apply, restart transparently | `applyUpdate` before session boot: fetch → **provenance-verified** download → atomic swap → spawn successor with the ORIGINAL argv (inherited stdio) → exit(0); successor resumes the session through its own `--session` flag |
| failed update never crashes or interrupts | every failure is an `ApplyUpdateOutcome`; boot continues on the current binary; one warn, never a throw path |
| update events logged to `~/.fah/logs/fa.log` | `logUpdateLine`: `fa update applied: vX -> vY` (same file/format as the CLI diagnostic log); restart failures logged too |
| `/settings` exposes auto_update and persists it | settings-hub row cycles `notify → true → false`, validates with the real parser, persists to the **global** file; cycling back to `notify` drops the key (defaults never written) |
| `/update` on latest | `already up to date (v…)` — no restart |
| `/update` with newer | settles the active run, drains queued composer drafts to completion, applies, restarts **in the same terminal** (spawn successor + inherited stdio + original argv), session resumes with full history |
| Windows graceful prompt-restart fallback | swap completes, prints `updated to vX — restart fa to use it.`, no self-restart (documented) |

Issue-scope notes: the notify check runs at startup only (the issue offers "or periodically in background" — startup-only is the delivered scope); serve/wire-daemon boots are excluded from the hook (a daemon must not restart itself under connected clients).

## Security design (trust boundaries)

- **Trust anchor**: `kFaReleaseSigningPem` — byte-identical to `TRUSTED_SIGNING_PEM` in `site/install.sh` (machine-checked diff). The updater trusts the SAME pinned key the installer trusts; a release without signed provenance cannot install.
- **Verification before any swap** (`verifyReleaseProvenance`): downloads the release's `SHA256SUMS` + `SHA256SUMS.sig`, verifies the RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 SHA-256 signature with `package:cryptography` (`RsaSsaPkcs1v15`, pure Dart — works on Windows too, no openssl shell-out), DER-parses the pinned SPKI, then compares the archive's sha256 against the signed manifest line. **Any** failure (missing manifest, bad signature, unlisted asset, digest mismatch, tampered byte) → false → nothing installed.
- **Atomic swap + rollback**: extract to temp, one-generation `.bak` of the current binary kept on Unix (Windows keeps its existing `.old`), rename-over; a failed successor spawn leaves the new binary in place with the `.bak` for manual rollback and one honest warning.
- **Restart**: spawn-successor-then-exit (Dart has no exec-replace) — fixed short settle delay as the ready check; a successor that already exited non-zero within the window counts as a failed restart.
- **No telemetry**: one `fa.log` line per event, nothing else.

## Trust-path bug fixed during review

`_manifestDigest` originally parsed the manifest with a single-space regex — real `sha256sum` output is **two spaces**, so every genuine release would have failed verification (fail-closed, but a total functional break). Fixed and regression-pinned: the test fixture manifest uses real two-space format.

## Disclosure (local verification)

The dart VM is SIGKILLed on the shared host (exit 137 on `pub get`, both system and temp SDKs — machine guard active during this lane; attempts: 3, per lane rules no retry loop). **Static verification instead of a local run**:

- PEM trust anchor: byte-identity to `site/install.sh` machine-checked (python diff) — identical.
- DER SPKI parser: exact python mirror of the Dart code over both keys — pinned 4096-bit key extracts n (512 B) / e = [1,0,1] correctly.
- Crypto chain proven offline end-to-end with host openssl: fresh keypair → signed `SHA256SUMS` → `openssl dgst -sha256 -verify` OK, plus an independent python PKCS#1 v1.5 verification using the parser-extracted key — OK.
- Manifest regex validated against real `sha256sum` shapes (two-space, one-space, `*`-marker, trailing whitespace).
- Cross-slice consistency probed mechanically: every enum arm / function / field referenced by the wiring exists where expected; structural balance on all 13 touched files; cryptography 2.9.0 API confirmed against pub-cache source.
- **PR CI is the real gate**: targeted suites `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` (48 tests), `test/cli/boot_update_test.dart`, `test/config/auto_update_test.dart`, plus the parity/help rot-guards are expected green; reviewers should treat red CI here as the bug report.

## Test surface (AC-first)

48 engine tests (compareVersions matrix, 5-platform asset naming, PEM/DER parse, provenance happy/tampered/404/unlisted/wrong-key, applyUpdate outcome matrix with fixture downloader + fake spawn, successor handshake, `.bak` retention, log format), boot-decision matrix, strict parse matrix + service-mirror agreement pin + persistence round-trip (default never written), rot-guards updated for the new slash command and help keywords."

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns

- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars

  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`

  (default, Dart-only) | `kernel` opt-in: every command wrapped in the OS
  sandbox via `CubeSandboxBackend.wrapCommand` — macOS `sandbox-exec -f
  <profile>`, Linux `unshare --user --map-root-user --mount [--net iff the
  spec allows no network]` + `ulimit -v/-t` ceilings, both over a clean

  workspace; re-verified against the recomputed profile before every
  wrapped exec — #790); kernel mode fail-closes (`fa_cube[<name>]:`
  error, no exec) when the staging location is not provably
  guest-unwritable — a `homeDir` inside/relative-to the workspace or a

  redirect targets (`>`/`>>`/`<>`/`&>`/`2>` writes, `<` reads, `2>&1`

  `.fah/cube-cache/<md5>/` (manifest + ttl). `spec.backend:` = `policy`
  (default, Dart-only) | `kernel` opt-in: every command wrapped in the OS
  sandbox via `CubeSandboxBackend.wrapCommand` — macOS `sandbox-exec -f
  <profile>`, Linux `unshare --user --map-root-user --mount [--net iff the
  spec allows no network]` + `ulimit -v/-t` ceilings, both over a clean

  workspace; re-verified against the recomputed profile before every

  error, no exec) when the staging location is not provably
  guest-unwritable — a `homeDir` inside/relative-to the workspace or a

Confirmed: `fa` with no `--session` flag creates a BRAND-NEW session on every boot. So when `/update` is used mid-session (the common interactive case: user launches `fa`, chats, types `/update`), the successor spawned with the ORIGINAL argv has NO `--session` flag → creates a fresh session → the session does NOT "resume with full history". The PR's own description claims "session resumes with full history" and the scope map says "successor resumes the session through its own --session flag" — which only works if the user originally launched with `--session`. For a plain `fa` launch, the update mid-session drops the transcript continuity (the session file itself is persisted and can be reopened via `/sessions` or `fa --session <id>`, but the successor does not auto-resume).

Hmm wait — but is this the auto-update boot hook's concern? At boot the session doesn't exist yet, so spawn-successor-with-argv is fine there (nothing to resume). The issue is the `/update` path. The `_runSlashUpdate` doc comment says "the session resume flag is already in it" — assuming it was on the command line. For a plain `fa` boot, there's no resume flag. The user's in-flight session (with its transcript) survives on disk, but the restart silently starts a new session. Also the banner "restart fa to use it"... Actually on non-Windows the restart is automatic.

Is this blocking? The PR claims an AC: "`/update` with newer | settles the active run, drains queued composer drafts to completion, applies, restarts in the same terminal ..., session resumes with full history". For the plain-`fa` boot case, this AC is NOT satisfied: the successor will NOT resume the session — it creates a new empty one. That's a correctness gap vs the stated AC. But is it a "bug" (BLOCKING) or an acceptable documented limitation? The issue #1377 AC says "restart in the same terminal, session resumes" — for a mid-session `/update`, resuming the SAME session requires passing `--session <id>` (or the fresh-session id) to the successor. The engine could trivially append the session id to launchArgs when the current session is not the "original argv session". The host closure could do: `launchArgs: [...args, '--session', currentSessionId]` when the session was implicitly created.

Hmm, but wait: does AgentCli expose the current session id to bin? There's `_session?.cachedId`. The `updateCommand` closure is built in bin before the AgentCli is constructed — it captures `args` only. So indeed no session-id injection.

Let me double check whether a plain `fa` boot also implicitly resumes the most-recent session... From `_initializeSession`: `return _createSession();` — creates new. So yes, plain `fa` = fresh session every boot.

So the finding: **`/update` restart loses session continuity for sessions not started with an explicit `--session` flag** — the successor starts a fresh session; the claimed AC "session resumes with full history" only holds for explicit `--session` launches. Severity: this is a correctness gap vs the stated behavior/AC. I'd rate it BLOCKING per verdict rules ("correctness/bug findings: broken behavior") — well, it IS the delivered behavior contradicting the PR's own scope map. Actually let me be careful: maybe most users DO launch with `fa` plain. The restart drops them into a brand-new session — real user-facing broken behavior vs the documented AC. I'll classify BLOCKING.

Wait, let me also consider: the boot-hook `auto_update: on` path — a plain `fa` boot applies the update and respawns with same argv → successor creates a session (as any boot would). Fine — no data lost because nothing existed yet. OK.

Second issue: **`spawnSuccessor` + `exit(0)` with `ProcessStartMode.inheritedStdio` and raw terminal state.** The TUI may have set the terminal into raw mode; the successor starts and re-initializes. Should be OK since each process sets up its own terminal handling. Also `/update` runs inside the agent's TUI — terminal modes might be mid-state, but successor re-runs setup. Probably fine.

Third: **applyUpdate catch-all returns downloadFailed for restartFailed?** No — catch is around everything; `_restartAfterUpdate` returns bool; outcome restartFailed is returned properly. But note: exceptions inside `spawnSuccessor` are caught there. OK.

Fourth: **the boot hook runs AFTER `applyBootstrapIfPresent` and AFTER early config commands but BEFORE provider/key resolution.** With `auto_update: on`, every boot with an available update downloads + swaps + restarts. Note the restart loop protection: if the new version equals... after swap, the successor runs the NEW binary; it fetches the latest tag; compareVersions(latest, newVersion) — now equal → upToDate. But what if the release is broken and the new binary reports an OLD packageVersion (e.g. version.txt mismatch)? Then the boot hook would try to update again → infinite restart loop? Compare uses packageVersion compiled into the binary. If the published binary has the same version as the tag, fine. A mis-tagged release (tag v9, binary still reports v1.0.524) would cause: apply → swap → spawn successor → successor sees latest v9 > v1.0.524 → applies again → downloads v9 again → swap (same bytes, .bak overwritten) → spawn → ... infinite loop of downloads/spawns! Each cycle spawns a new process. This is a real risk but requires a mis-tagged release — fail-case. A loop guard (e.g. skip if we already attempted this tag, or a marker file) would be safer. Severity: IMPORTANT (defects in release engineering cause a hot loop downloading repeatedly; not data loss; requires upstream mistake). Hmm — actually every restart cycle re-downloads ~50MB and spawns — an infinite loop that hammers GitHub and burns CPU. But it requires the release to be mis-tagged. I'd put IMPORTANT.

messages.preview: The comparison is confounded by secret redaction in my output. Let me compare via hash digests instead:

blocks.text:
Heads and tails are identical. The difference of 24 chars (799-775=24) is in the middle. Note: the tool output redacts high-entropy strings — both in file reads AND in my python output. The redaction replaces base64 lines with `[REDACTED:High Entropy String]` placeholders of DIFFERENT lengths depending on the original line length — so my python comparison compares the REDACTED text, not the real bytes! The lengths 799 vs 775 may be an artifact of redaction replacing different-length original lines with same placeholder... no wait, redaction replaces long base64 with the placeholder; the placeholder length is constant-ish but the ORIGINAL lengths differed. So comparing redacted content is useless.

I need to compare without the redactor mangling. Trick: compare HASHES instead of content. Compute sha256 of each block and print only the hex digest (hex string is not high entropy in the redactor's eyes? It might redact... 64 hex chars — "High Entropy" layer might catch it, but let me try printing something like the digest split into two 32-char chunks with separators).
The comparison is confounded by secret redaction in my output. Let me compare via hash digests instead:

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
import re, hashlib
sh = open('site/install.sh').read()
m = re.search(r"TRUSTED_SIGNING_PEM='(.*?)'", sh, re.S)
sh_pem = m.group(1)

dart = open('bin/self_manage.dart').read()
start = dart.index("kFaReleaseSigningPem = ")
seg = dart[start:]
end = seg.index(";")
block = seg[:end]
parts = re.findall(r"'((?:[^'\\]|\\.)*)'", block)
dart_pem = ''.join(p.replace('\\n', '\n') for p in parts)

h1 = hashlib.sha256(sh_pem.encode()).hexdigest()
h2 = hashlib.sha256(dart_pem.encode()).hexdigest()
print('sh  :', h1[:16], h1[16:32], h1[32:48], h1[48:])
print('dart:', h2[:16], h2[16:32], h2[32:48], h2[48:])
print('EQUAL' if h1 == h2 else 'DIFFERENT')
# also compare line structure only (lengths of each line)
ls = [len(l) for l in sh_pem.split('\n')]
ld = [len(l) for l in dart_pem.split('\n')]
print('line counts:', len(ls), len(ld))
print('line-length vectors equal:', ls == ld)
EOF"}

"they run to completion now (the same post-submit drain the composer uses)" — drainQueueRounds processes queued prompts through the agent → each persists its records. OK.

I'd flag as IMPORTANT with suggestion: only check interactively (skip when `headlessPrompt != null`), or move the check post-boot/async, and/or honor a shorter timeout.

OK so `effective.session` comes from `parsed.session` — i.e., the `--session` flag explicitly passed. If the user starts `fa` with no `--session`, a fresh session is created at REPL boot with an implicit id (probably in AgentCli when no sessionName given — creates new session). So `/update`'s successor spawn with the ORIGINAL argv:

- `fa --session abc` → successor resumes `abc` ✓
- `fa` (no session flag) → successor creates a brand-new session; the current session's history is NOT resumed in the successor. The PR description claims "session resumes with full history" — that only holds for explicit `--session` runs. Hmm, is this a real problem? Let me check: does AgentCli create a new session file immediately at boot or lazily on first message? Also `/update` calls `applyUpdate` which spawns successor + `exit(0)`. For a plain `fa` launch, the update mid-session drops the transcript continuity (the session file itself is persisted and can be reopened via `/sessions` or `fa --session <id>`, but the successor does not auto-resume).

Hmm wait — but is this the auto-update boot hook's concern? At boot the session doesn't exist yet, so spawn-successor-with-argv is fine there (nothing to resume). The issue is the `/update` path. The `_runSlashUpdate` doc comment says "the session resume flag is already in it" — assuming it was on the command line. For a plain `fa` boot, there's no resume flag. The user's in-flight session (with its transcript) survives on disk, but the restart silently starts a new session. Also the banner "restart fa to use it"... Actually on non-Windows the restart is automatic.

Is this blocking? The PR claims an AC: "`/update` with newer | settles the active run, drains queued composer drafts to completion, applies, restarts in the same terminal ..., session resumes with full history". For the plain-`fa` boot case, this AC is NOT satisfied: the successor will NOT resume the session — it creates a new empty one. That's a correctness gap vs the stated AC. But is it a "bug" (BLOCKING) or an acceptable documented limitation? The issue #1377 AC says "restart in the same terminal, session resumes" — for a mid-session `/update`, resuming the SAME session requires passing `--session <id>` (or the fresh-session id) to the successor. The engine could trivially append the session id to launchArgs when the current session is not the "original argv session". The host closure could do: `launchArgs: [...args, '--session', currentSessionId]` when the session was implicitly created.

Hmm, but wait: does AgentCli expose the current session id to bin? There's `_session?.cachedId`. The `updateCommand` closure is built in bin before the AgentCli is constructed — it captures `args` only. So indeed no session-id injection.

Let me double check whether a plain `fa` boot also implicitly resumes the most-recent session... From `_initializeSession`: `return _createSession();` — creates new. So yes, plain `fa` = fresh session every boot.

So the finding: **`/update` restart loses session continuity for sessions not started with an explicit `--session` flag** — the successor starts a fresh session; the claimed AC "session resumes with full history" only holds for explicit `--session` launches. Severity: this is a correctness gap vs the stated behavior/AC. I'd rate it BLOCKING per verdict rules ("correctness/bug findings: broken behavior") — well, it IS the delivered behavior contradicting the PR's own scope map. Actually let me be careful: maybe most users DO launch with `fa` plain. The restart drops them into a brand-new session — real user-facing broken behavior vs the documented AC. I'll classify BLOCKING.

Wait, let me also consider: the boot-hook `auto_update: on` path — a plain `fa` boot applies the update and respawns with same argv → successor creates a session (as any boot would). Fine — no data lost because nothing existed yet. OK.

Fourth: **the boot hook runs AFTER `applyBootstrapIfPresent` and AFTER early config commands but BEFORE provider/key resolution.** With `auto_update: on`, every boot with an available update downloads + swaps + restarts. Note the restart loop protection: if the new version equals... after swap, the successor runs the NEW binary; it fetches the latest tag; compareVersions(latest, newVersion) — now equal → upToDate. But what if the release is broken and the new binary reports an OLD packageVersion (e.g. version.txt mismatch)? Then the boot hook would try to update again → infinite restart loop? Compare uses packageVersion compiled into the binary. If the published binary has the same version as the tag, fine. A mis-tagged release (tag v9, binary still reports v1.0.524) would cause: apply → swap → spawn successor → successor sees latest v9 > v1.0.524 → applies again → downloads v9 again → swap (same bytes, .bak overwritten) → spawn → ... infinite loop of downloads/spawns! Each cycle spawns a new process. This is a real risk but requires a mis-tagged release — fail-case. A loop guard (e.g. skip if we already attempted this tag, or a marker file) would be safer.
