Confirmed: `fa` with no `--session` flag creates a BRAND-NEW session on every boot. So when `/update` is used mid-session (the common interactive case: user launches `fa`, chats, types `/update`), the successor spawned with the ORIGINAL argv has NO `--session` flag → creates a fresh session → the session does NOT "resume with full history". The PR's own description claims "session resumes with full history" and the scope map says "successor resumes the session through its own --session flag" — which only works if the user originally launched with `--session`. For a plain `fa` launch, the update mid-session drops the transcript continuity (the session file itself is persisted and can be reopened via `/sessions` or `fa --session <id>`, but the successor does not auto-resume).

Hmm wait — but is this the auto-update boot hook's concern? At boot the session doesn't exist yet, so spawn-successor-with-argv is fine there (nothing to resume). The issue is the `/update` path. The `_runSlashUpdate` doc comment says "the session resume flag is already in it" — assuming it was on the command line. For a plain `fa` boot, there's no resume flag. The user's in-flight session (with its transcript) survives on disk, but the restart silently starts a new session. Also the banner "restart fa to use it"... Actually on non-Windows the restart is automatic.

Is this blocking? The PR claims an AC: "`/update` with newer | settles the active run, drains queued composer drafts to completion, applies, restarts in the same terminal ..., session resumes with full history". For the plain-`fa` boot case, this AC is NOT satisfied: the successor will NOT resume the session — it creates a new empty one. That's a correctness gap vs the stated AC. But is it a "bug" (BLOCKING) or an acceptable documented limitation? The issue #1377 AC says "restart in the same terminal, session resumes" — for a mid-session `/update`, resuming the SAME session requires passing `--session <id>` (or the fresh-session id) to the successor. The engine could trivially append the session id to launchArgs when the current session is not the "original argv session". The host closure could do: `launchArgs: [...args, '--session', currentSessionId]` when the session was implicitly created.

Hmm, but wait: does AgentCli expose the current session id to bin? There's `_session?.cachedId`. The `updateCommand` closure is built in bin before the AgentCli is constructed — it captures `args` only. So indeed no session-id injection.

Let me double check whether a plain `fa` boot also implicitly resumes the most-recent session... From `_initializeSession`: `return _createSession();` — creates new. So yes, plain `fa` = fresh session every boot.

So the finding: **`/update` restart loses session continuity for sessions not started with an explicit `--session` flag** — the successor starts a fresh session; the claimed AC "session resumes with full history" only holds for explicit `--session` launches. Severity: this is a correctness gap vs the stated behavior/AC. I'd rate it BLOCKING per verdict rules ("correctness/bug findings: broken behavior") — well, it IS the delivered behavior contradicting the PR's own scope map. Actually let me be careful: maybe most users DO launch with `fa` plain. The restart drops them into a brand-new session — real user-facing broken behavior vs the documented AC. I'll classify BLOCKING.

Wait, let me also consider: the boot-hook `auto_update: on` path — a plain `fa` boot applies the update and respawns with same argv → successor creates a session (as any boot would). Fine — no data lost because nothing existed yet. OK.

Second issue: **`spawnSuccessor` + `exit(0)` with `ProcessStartMode.inheritedStdio` and raw terminal state.** The TUI may have set the terminal into raw mode; the successor starts and re-initializes. Should be OK since each process sets up its own terminal handling. Also `/update` runs inside the agent's TUI — terminal modes might be mid-state, but successor re-runs setup. Probably fine.

Third: **applyUpdate catch-all returns downloadFailed for restartFailed?** No — catch is around everything; `_restartAfterUpdate` returns bool; outcome restartFailed is returned properly. But note: exceptions inside `spawnSuccessor` are caught there. OK.

Fourth: **the boot hook runs AFTER `applyBootstrapIfPresent` and AFTER early config commands but BEFORE provider/key resolution.** With `auto_update: on`, every boot with an available update downloads + swaps + restarts. Note the restart loop protection: if the new version equals... after swap, the successor runs the NEW binary; it fetches the latest tag; compareVersions(latest, newVersion) — now equal → upToDate. But what if the release is broken and the new binary reports an OLD packageVersion (e.g. version.txt mismatch)? Then the boot hook would try to update again → infinite restart loop? Compare uses packageVersion compiled into the binary. If the published binary has the same version as the tag, fine. A mis-tagged release (tag v9, binary still reports v1.0.524) would cause: apply → swap → spawn successor → successor sees latest v9 > v1.0.524 → applies again → downloads v9 again → swap (same bytes, .bak overwritten) → spawn → ... infinite loop of downloads/spawns! Each cycle spawns a new process. This is a real risk but requires a mis-tagged release — fail-case. A loop guard (e.g. skip if we already attempted this tag, or a marker file) would be safer. Severity: IMPORTANT (defects in release engineering cause a hot loop downloading repeatedly; not data loss; requires upstream mistake). Hmm — actually every restart cycle re-downloads ~50MB and spawns — an infinite loop that hammers GitHub and burns CPU. But it requires the release to be mis-tagged. I'd put IMPORTANT.

Fifth: **`fetchLatestTag().timeout(3s)` in notify path leaks the client** — on timeout the underlying HTTP request is abandoned; client never closed (fetchLatestTag created its own client; the `.timeout` fires, the function's `finally` won't run until the underlying send completes — actually no! The `finally` in `fetchLatestTag` is inside the future that `.timeout` wraps; when timeout fires, the original future keeps running — the client stays open until the request eventually completes/errors. The socket eventually closes when the request errors (TCP timeout could be 2+ min). It's a per-boot transient leak — minor. SUGGESTION.

Also — the notify check adds up to 3 s to EVERY boot (interactive and headless alike) when the endpoint is slow/dead. In `notify` mode the default, every run pays a network round-trip before session boot. `timeout` 3 s. Headless runs in CI would also do this network fetch — CI determinism/no-network concerns! `auto_update` default is `notify` — every `fa -p "..."` run in a sandboxed CI without network will wait up to 3 s per invocation and spam stderr? No — banner only prints when a newer version is found; failures silent. But the 3-second boot delay for headless runs with no network (connect timeout) is real: each `fa -p` invocation stalls 3 s. That's a UX/perf concern — IMPORTANT? The AC says "non-blocking banner" — it does block the boot up to 3 s. The PR acknowledges "bounded (~3 s)". Hmm. It's within the stated design. I'd rate SUGGESTION/note. Actually think: default `notify` — silently added network traffic on every boot for ALL users (privacy/behavior change; "zero network" only for off). The PR does document this. I'll note it as a suggestion-level concern (skip via timeout only; maybe make the check async post-boot). Not blocking.

blocks.text:
Confirmed: `fa` with no `--session` flag creates a BRAND-NEW session on every boot. So when `/update` is used mid-session (the common interactive case: user launches `fa`, chats, types `/update`), the successor spawned with the ORIGINAL argv has NO `--session` flag → creates a fresh session → the session does NOT "resume with full history". The PR's own description claims "session resumes with full history" and the scope map says "successor resumes the session through its own --session flag" — which only works if the user originally launched with `--session`. For a plain `fa` launch, the update mid-session drops the transcript continuity (the session file itself is persisted and can be reopened via `/sessions` or `fa --session <id>`, but the successor does not auto-resume).

Hmm wait — but is this the auto-update boot hook's concern? At boot the session doesn't exist yet, so spawn-successor-with-argv is fine there (nothing to resume). The issue is the `/update` path. The `_runSlashUpdate` doc comment says "the session resume flag is already in it" — assuming it was on the command line. For a plain `fa` boot, there's no resume flag. The user's in-flight session (with its transcript) survives on disk, but the restart silently starts a new session. Also the banner "restart fa to use it"... Actually on non-Windows the restart is automatic.

Is this blocking? The PR claims an AC: "`/update` with newer | settles the active run, drains queued composer drafts to completion, applies, restarts in the same terminal ..., session resumes with full history". For the plain-`fa` boot case, this AC is NOT satisfied: the successor will NOT resume the session — it creates a new empty one. That's a correctness gap vs the stated AC. But is it a "bug" (BLOCKING) or an acceptable documented limitation? The issue #1377 AC says "restart in the same terminal, session resumes" — for a mid-session `/update`, resuming the SAME session requires passing `--session <id>` (or the fresh-session id) to the successor. The engine could trivially append the session id to launchArgs when the current session is not the "original argv session". The host closure could do: `launchArgs: [...args, '--session', currentSessionId]` when the session was implicitly created.

Hmm, but wait: does AgentCli expose the current session id to bin? There's `_session?.cachedId`. The `updateCommand` closure is built in bin before the AgentCli is constructed — it captures `args` only. So indeed no session-id injection.

Let me double check whether a plain `fa` boot also implicitly resumes the most-recent session... From `_initializeSession`: `return _createSession();` — creates new. So yes, plain `fa` = fresh session every boot.

So the finding: **`/update` restart loses session continuity for sessions not started with an explicit `--session` flag** — the successor starts a fresh session; the claimed AC "session resumes with full history" only holds for explicit `--session` launches. Severity: this is a correctness gap vs the stated behavior/AC. I'd rate it BLOCKING per verdict rules ("correctness/bug findings: broken behavior") — well, it IS the delivered behavior contradicting the PR's own scope map. Actually let me be careful: maybe most users DO launch with `fa` plain. The restart drops them into a brand-new session — real user-facing broken behavior vs the documented AC. I'll classify BLOCKING.

Wait, let me also consider: the boot-hook `auto_update: on` path — a plain `fa` boot applies the update and respawns with same argv → successor creates a session (as any boot would). Fine — no data lost because nothing existed yet. OK.

# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo: 12.0 (re-measured whole-tree on
  # the merged-suite lcov, #1234 rework). The card's named offenders DID
  # move — readPasteboardImage 16.32 (split into fake-seam /
  # platform-dispatch helpers), the CC-12 trio (_handleTreeKey,
  # discoverTaskAgents, _rebuild) split into cohesive sub-dispatchers,
  # the four 0%-cov CC-3 methods covered by tests (frontmatter, video
  # endpoint, below-window ingest, provider picker), the named CC-9 tier
  # split, and _listModels (20 @ 0%) covered by the line-mode /models
  # test. But the FIRST real whole-tree measurement (the authoring box
  # had no dart toolchain) shows the 12.0 → 8.0 repin is not earned yet:
  # 137 methods measure above 8.0 — 54 at exactly 12.00 (the CC-3 @ 0%
  # tier + fully-covered CC-12 dispatchers) and 83 at 9.00 (CC-9 @ 100%).
  # Threshold stays at the measured max; the 12.00/9.00 tier is the next
  # ladder card (cover the CC-3@0% half, split the CC-12 dispatchers,
  # then the threshold follows down to 8.0). Only down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
  # _listModels used to hit 20 with 0% coverage (line-mode-only output);
  # covered by test/cli/provider_models_line_mode_test.dart in #1234.

# ─── loc gate (issue #1234, gh-1232 migration) ─────────────────────────────
# The ≤2800-line file guard MOVED from scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_size +
# the ci.yml shell find-exec guards onto crap4dart's `loc` gate (0.11.0,
# maintainer-confirmed wc -l semantics). Enforced whole-tree on every merge
# validation via `crap4dart check --baseline` (CI quality-gates step) and
# staged files in the pre-commit hook — no staged-scoping escape, no
# hook-dependence, merge-bot merges included. max_lines only DOWN;
# app_localizations.dart is gen-l10n OUTPUT (no .g.dart suffix) — excluded,
# not baselined.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  # Issue #1234: the whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was stage_size +
  # ci.yml shell find-exec, gh-1232). wc -l semantics, generated output
  # excluded — nothing exceeds 2800 today, so the shrink-only baseline
  # starts EMPTY of loc entries. Scope = the package sources [lib, bin]:
  # 0.11.0 has NO per-gate sources override (gates.loc.sources is a
  # ConfigException — caught by CI on 019ede65), and the top-level
  # sources drive the CRAP census too, so they stay untouched. test/ and
  # example/ are enforced by the companion config
  # crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml (same loc gate, sources [test, example]);
  # the app package's own config covers flutter_app/lib.
  loc:
    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - '**.g.dart'
      - '**.freezed.dart'
      - '**.mocks.dart'
      - 'vendor/**'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false} # follow-up card (issue #1234 §5). Known
    # FPs to exclude when enabling: the conditional-export IO entry points
    # (lib/io.dart, lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart — public barrels whose
    # importers live outside this repo's import graph) and shared pinned
    # data modules imported only from test/ (lib/src/cli/omp_reg_scenarios.dart,
    # issue #810). lib/fanet.dart was the one confirmed-dead hit — deleted
    # in #1234.
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  #
  # Two suppression channels with different contracts:
  # - `// crap:ignore` (needs ignorable: true) = a JUSTIFIED structural
  #   twin, suppressed forever, with a one-line reason in the comment.
  # - `.crap-baseline.json` (via `check --baseline`) = LEGACY debt; the
  #   committed snapshot must only SHRINK: after each triage batch re-run
  #   `dart pub global run crap4dart check --save-baseline` and commit the
  #   only-down diff, or the snapshot rots and starts masking shifts.
  #
  # WINDOW (until severity flips to error): the gate never fails a build —
  # new (not-baselined) duplication only surfaces as a `[WARN]` line in
  # `check` output. Enforcement becomes hard exactly when the owner-side
  # escalation lands; from then on any finding outside the two channels
  # fails CI/pre-commit.
  duplication:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out
    sources: # cross-module scope from #487
      - flutter_app/lib
      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:
      # TUI screenshots, not goldens: amber/yellow text on the dark theme
      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for
      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.
      - 'test/integration/**'
---
# crap4dart loc-scope companion configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (issue #1234 rework): crap4dart 0.11.0 has no
# per-gate `sources` override — `gates.loc.sources` is rejected as an
# unknown key (ConfigException; caught by CI on 019ede65). The package
# config's top-level `sources` drives the CRAP census too, so it must
# stay [lib, bin]. This companion config runs the SAME loc gate over the
# one slice the package config cannot express: test/ + example/ — the
# exact scope the retired shell guards (gh-1232 stage_size + the ci.yml
# find-exec jobs) scanned there. flutter_app/lib stays under
# flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
#
# RATCHET: max_lines mirrors both package configs (2800, wc -l
# semantics, generated output excluded); max_lines only DOWN.
# Enforcement: whole-tree in CI (guards job, `check --config` step) and
# staged files in scripts/pre-commit — the same two points as the
# package configs.

sources: [test, example]
---
.github/workflows/ci.yml:133:          [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ] && stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
.github/workflows/ci.yml:142:            stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
.github/workflows/ci.yml:249:      # Issue #1234: the ≤2800-line file guard MOVED into crap4dart's loc
.github/workflows/ci.yml:250:      # gate (crap4dart.yaml, wc -l parity verified by the maintainer
.github/workflows/ci.yml:252:      # `crap4dart check --baseline` Quality-gates step below. The shell
.github/workflows/ci.yml:302:      # Issue #433 AC1: README CRAP badge must equal the crap4dart.yaml
.github/workflows/ci.yml:307:        run: python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py
.github/workflows/ci.yml:1124:      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in crap4dart.yaml)
.github/workflows/ci.yml:1139:          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.11.0 <0.12.0"
.github/workflows/ci.yml:1140:          dart pub global run crap4dart analyze

blocks.text:
Confirmed: `fa` with no `--session` flag creates a BRAND-NEW session on every boot. So when `/update` is used mid-session (the common interactive case: user launches `fa`, chats, types `/update`), the successor spawned with the ORIGINAL argv has NO `--session` flag → creates a fresh session → the session does NOT "resume with full history". The PR's own description claims "session resumes with full history" and the scope map says "successor resumes the session through its own --session flag" — which only works if the user originally launched with `--session`. For a plain `fa` launch, the update mid-session drops the transcript continuity (the session file itself is persisted and can be reopened via `/sessions` or `fa --session <id>`, but the successor does not auto-resume).

Hmm wait — but is this the auto-update boot hook's concern? At boot the session doesn't exist yet, so spawn-successor-with-argv is fine there (nothing to resume). The issue is the `/update` path. The `_runSlashUpdate` doc comment says "the session resume flag is already in it" — assuming it was on the command line. For a plain `fa` boot, there's no resume flag. The user's in-flight session (with its transcript) survives on disk, but the restart silently starts a new session. Also the banner "restart fa to use it"... Actually on non-Windows the restart is automatic.

Is this blocking? The PR claims an AC: "`/update` with newer | settles the active run, drains queued composer drafts to completion, applies, restarts in the same terminal ..., session resumes with full history". For the plain-`fa` boot case, this AC is NOT satisfied: the successor will NOT resume the session — it creates a new empty one. That's a correctness gap vs the stated AC. But is it a "bug" (BLOCKING) or an acceptable documented limitation? The issue #1377 AC says "restart in the same terminal, session resumes" — for a mid-session `/update`, resuming the SAME session requires passing `--session <id>` (or the fresh-session id) to the successor. The engine could trivially append the session id to launchArgs when the current session is not the "original argv session". The host closure could do: `launchArgs: [...args, '--session', currentSessionId]` when the session was implicitly created.

Hmm, but wait: does AgentCli expose the current session id to bin? There's `_session?.cachedId`. The `updateCommand` closure is built in bin before the AgentCli is constructed — it captures `args` only. So indeed no session-id injection.

Let me double check whether a plain `fa` boot also implicitly resumes the most-recent session... From `_initializeSession`: `return _createSession();` — creates new. So yes, plain `fa` = fresh session every boot.

So the finding: **`/update` restart loses session continuity for sessions not started with an explicit `--session` flag** — the successor starts a fresh session; the claimed AC "session resumes with full history" only holds for explicit `--session` launches. Severity: this is a correctness gap vs the stated behavior/AC. I'd rate it BLOCKING per verdict rules ("correctness/bug findings: broken behavior") — well, it IS the delivered behavior contradicting the PR's own scope map. Actually let me be careful: maybe most users DO launch with `fa` plain. The restart drops them into a brand-new session — real user-facing broken behavior vs the documented AC. I'll classify BLOCKING.

Wait, let me also consider: the boot-hook `auto_update: on` path — a plain `fa` boot applies the update and respawns with same argv → successor creates a session (as any boot would). Fine — no data lost because nothing existed yet. OK.

Second issue: **`spawnSuccessor` + `exit(0)` with `ProcessStartMode.inheritedStdio` and raw terminal state.** The TUI may have set the terminal into raw mode; the successor starts and re-initializes. Should be OK since each process sets up its own terminal handling. Also `/update` runs inside the agent's TUI — terminal modes might be mid-state, but successor re-runs setup. Probably fine.

# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo: 12.0 (re-measured whole-tree on
  # the merged-suite lcov, #1234 rework). The card's named offenders DID
  # move — readPasteboardImage 16.32 (split into fake-seam /
  # platform-dispatch helpers), the CC-12 trio (_handleTreeKey,
  # discoverTaskAgents, _rebuild) split into cohesive sub-dispatchers,
  # the four 0%-cov CC-3 methods covered by tests (frontmatter, video
  # endpoint, below-window ingest, provider picker), the named CC-9 tier
  # split, and _listModels (20 @ 0%) covered by the line-mode /models
  # test. But the FIRST real whole-tree measurement (the authoring box
  # had no dart toolchain) shows the 12.0 → 8.0 repin is not earned yet:
  # 137 methods measure above 8.0 — 54 at exactly 12.00 (the CC-3 @ 0%
  # tier + fully-covered CC-12 dispatchers) and 83 at 9.00 (CC-9 @ 100%).
  # Threshold stays at the measured max; the 12.00/9.00 tier is the next
  # ladder card (cover the CC-3@0% half, split the CC-12 dispatchers,
  # then the threshold follows down to 8.0). Only down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
  # _listModels used to hit 20 with 0% coverage (line-mode-only output);
  # covered by test/cli/provider_models_line_mode_test.dart in #1234.

# ─── loc gate (issue #1234, gh-1232 migration) ─────────────────────────────
# The ≤2800-line file guard MOVED from scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_size +
# the ci.yml shell find-exec guards onto crap4dart's `loc` gate (0.11.0,
# maintainer-confirmed wc -l semantics). Enforced whole-tree on every merge
# validation via `crap4dart check --baseline` (CI quality-gates step) and
# staged files in the pre-commit hook — no staged-scoping escape, no
# hook-dependence, merge-bot merges included. max_lines only DOWN;
# app_localizations.dart is gen-l10n OUTPUT (no .g.dart suffix) — excluded,
# not baselined.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  # Issue #1234: the whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was stage_size +
  # ci.yml shell find-exec, gh-1232). wc -l semantics, generated output
  # excluded — nothing exceeds 2800 today, so the shrink-only baseline
  # starts EMPTY of loc entries. Scope = the package sources [lib, bin]:
  # 0.11.0 has NO per-gate sources override (gates.loc.sources is a
  # ConfigException — caught by CI on 019ede65), and the top-level
  # sources drive the CRAP census too, so they stay untouched. test/ and
  # example/ are enforced by the companion config
  # crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml (same loc gate, sources [test, example]);
  # the app package's own config covers flutter_app/lib.
  loc:
    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - '**.g.dart'
      - '**.freezed.dart'
      - '**.mocks.dart'
      - 'vendor/**'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false} # follow-up card (issue #1234 §5). Known
    # FPs to exclude when enabling: the conditional-export IO entry points
    # (lib/io.dart, lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart — public barrels whose
    # importers live outside this repo's import graph) and shared pinned
    # data modules imported only from test/ (lib/src/cli/omp_reg_scenarios.dart,
    # issue #810). lib/fanet.dart was the one confirmed-dead hit — deleted
    # in #1234.
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  #
  # Two suppression channels with different contracts:
  # - `// crap:ignore` (needs ignorable: true) = a JUSTIFIED structural
  #   twin, suppressed forever, with a one-line reason in the comment.
  # - `.crap-baseline.json` (via `check --baseline`) = LEGACY debt; the
  #   committed snapshot must only SHRINK: after each triage batch re-run
  #   `dart pub global run crap4dart check --save-baseline` and commit the
  #   only-down diff, or the snapshot rots and starts masking shifts.
  #
  # WINDOW (until severity flips to error): the gate never fails a build —
  # new (not-baselined) duplication only surfaces as a `[WARN]` line in
  # `check` output. Enforcement becomes hard exactly when the owner-side
  # escalation lands; from then on any finding outside the two channels
  # fails CI/pre-commit.
  duplication:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out
    sources: # cross-module scope from #487
      - flutter_app/lib
      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:
      # TUI screenshots, not goldens: amber/yellow text on the dark theme
      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for
      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.
      - 'test/integration/**'
---
# crap4dart loc-scope companion configuration for flutter_agent_harness.

# unknown key (ConfigException; caught by CI on 019ede65). The package
# config's top-level `sources` drives the CRAP census too, so it must
# stay [lib, bin]. This companion config runs the SAME loc gate over the
# one slice the package config cannot express: test/ + example/ — the
# exact scope the retired shell guards (gh-1232 stage_size + the ci.yml
# find-exec jobs) scanned there. flutter_app/lib stays under
# flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
#
# RATCHET: max_lin…

# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo: 12.0 (re-measured whole-tree on
  # the merged-suite lcov, #1234 rework). The card's named offenders DID
  # move — readPasteboardImage 16.32 (split into fake-seam /
  # platform-dispatch helpers), the CC-12 trio (_handleTreeKey,
  # discoverTaskAgents, _rebuild) split into cohesive sub-dispatchers,
  # the four 0%-cov CC-3 methods covered by tests (frontmatter, video
  # endpoint, below-window ingest, provider picker), the named CC-9 tier
  # split, and _listModels (20 @ 0%) covered by the line-mode /models
  # test. But the FIRST real whole-tree measurement (the authoring box
  # had no dart toolchain) shows the 12.0 → 8.0 repin is not earned yet:
  # 137 methods measure above 8.0 — 54 at exactly 12.00 (the CC-3 @ 0%
  # tier + fully-covered CC-12 dispatchers) and 83 at 9.00 (CC-9 @ 100%).
  # Threshold stays at the measured max; the 12.00/9.00 tier is the next
  # ladder card (cover the CC-3@0% half, split the CC-12 dispatchers,
  # then the threshold follows down to 8.0). Only down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
  # _listModels used to hit 20 with 0% coverage (line-mode-only output);
  # covered by test/cli/provider_models_line_mode_test.dart in #1234.

# ─── loc gate (issue #1234, gh-1232 migration) ─────────────────────────────
# The ≤2800-line file guard MOVED from scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_size +
# the ci.yml shell find-exec guards onto crap4dart's `loc` gate (0.11.0,
# maintainer-confirmed wc -l semantics). Enforced whole-tree on every merge
# validation via `crap4dart check --baseline` (CI quality-gates step) and
# staged files in the pre-commit hook — no staged-scoping escape, no
# hook-dependence, merge-bot merges included. max_lines only DOWN;
# app_localizations.dart is gen-l10n OUTPUT (no .g.dart suffix) — excluded,
# not baselined.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  # Issue #1234: the whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was stage_size +
  # ci.yml shell find-exec, gh-1232). wc -l semantics, generated output
  # excluded — nothing exceeds 2800 today, so the shrink-only baseline
  # starts EMPTY of loc entries. Scope = the package sources [lib, bin]:
  # 0.11.0 has NO per-gate sources override (gates.loc.sources is a
  # ConfigException — caught by CI on 019ede65), and the top-level
  # sources drive the CRAP census too, so they stay untouched. test/ and
  # example/ are enforced by the companion config
  # crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml (same loc gate, sources [test, example]);
  # the app package's own config covers flutter_app/lib.
  loc:
    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - '**.g.dart'
      - '**.freezed.dart'
      - '**.mocks.dart'
      - 'vendor/**'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false} # follow-up card (issue #1234 §5). Known
    # FPs to exclude when enabling: the conditional-export IO entry points
    # (lib/io.dart, lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart — public barrels whose
    # importers live outside this repo's import graph) and shared pinned
    # data modules imported only from test/ (lib/src/cli/omp_reg_scenarios.dart,
    # issue #810). lib/fanet.dart was the one confirmed-dead hit — deleted
    # in #1234.
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  #
  # Two suppression channels with different contracts:
  # - `// crap:ignore` (needs ignorable: true) = a JUSTIFIED structural
  #   twin, suppressed forever, with a one-line reason in the comment.
  # - `.crap-baseline.json` (via `check --baseline`) = LEGACY debt; the
  #   committed snapshot must only SHRINK: after each triage batch re-run
  #   `dart pub global run crap4dart check --save-baseline` and commit the
  #   only-down diff, or the snapshot rots and starts masking shifts.
  #
  # WINDOW (until severity flips to error): the gate never fails a build —
  # new (not-baselined) duplication only surfaces as a `[WARN]` line in
  # `check` output. Enforcement becomes hard exactly when the owner-side
  # escalation lands; from then on any finding outside the two channels
  # fails CI/pre-commit.
  duplication:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out
    sources: # cross-module scope from #487
      - flutter_app/lib
      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:
      # TUI screenshots, not goldens: amber/yellow text on the dark theme
      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for
      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.
      - 'test/integration/**'

# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo: 12.0 (re-measured whole-tree on
  # the merged-suite lcov, #1234 rework). The card's named offenders DID
  # move — readPasteboardImage 16.32 (split into fake-seam /
  # platform-dispatch helpers), the CC-12 trio (_handleTreeKey,
  # discoverTaskAgents, _rebuild) split into cohesive sub-dispatchers,
  # the four 0%-cov CC-3 methods covered by tests (frontmatter, video
  # endpoint, below-window ingest, provider picker), the named CC-9 tier
  # split, and _listModels (20 @ 0%) covered by the line-mode /models
  # test. But the FIRST real whole-tree measurement (the authoring box
  # had no dart toolchain) shows the 12.0 → 8.0 repin is not earned yet:
  # 137 methods measure above 8.0 — 54 at exactly 12.00 (the CC-3 @ 0%
  # tier + fully-covered CC-12 dispatchers) and 83 at 9.00 (CC-9 @ 100%).
  # Threshold stays at the measured max; the 12.00/9.00 tier is the next
  # ladder card (cover the CC-3@0% half, split the CC-12 dispatchers,
  # then the threshold follows down to 8.0). Only down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
  # _listModels used to hit 20 with 0% coverage (line-mode-only output);
  # covered by test/cli/provider_models_line_mode_test.dart in #1234.

# ─── loc gate (issue #1234, gh-1232 migration) ─────────────────────────────
# The ≤2800-line file guard MOVED from scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_size +
# the ci.yml shell find-exec guards onto crap4dart's `loc` gate (0.11.0,
# maintainer-confirmed wc -l semantics). Enforced whole-tree on every merge
# validation via `crap4dart check --baseline` (CI quality-gates step) and
# staged files in the pre-commit hook — no staged-scoping escape, no
# hook-dependence, merge-bot merges included. max_lines only DOWN;
# app_localizations.dart is gen-l10n OUTPUT (no .g.dart suffix) — excluded,
# not baselined.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  # Issue #1234: the whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was stage_size +
  # ci.yml shell find-exec, gh-1232). wc -l semantics, generated output
  # excluded — nothing exceeds 2800 today, so the shrink-only baseline
  # starts EMPTY of loc entries. Scope = the package sources [lib, bin]:
  # 0.11.0 has NO per-gate sources override (gates.loc.sources is a
  # ConfigException — caught by CI on 019ede65), and the top-level
  # sources drive the CRAP census too, so they stay untouched. test/ and
  # example/ are enforced by the companion config
  # crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml (same loc gate, sources [test, example]);
  # the app package's own config covers flutter_app/lib.
  loc:
    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - '**.g.dart'
      - '**.freezed.dart'
      - '**.mocks.dart'
      - 'vendor/**'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false} # follow-up card (issue #1234 §5). Known
    # FPs to exclude when enabling: the conditional-export IO entry points
    # (lib/io.dart, lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart — public barrels whose
    # importers live outside this repo's import graph) and shared pinned
    # data modules imported only from test/ (lib/src/cli/omp_reg_scenarios.dart,
    # issue #810). lib/fanet.dart was the one confirmed-dead hit — deleted
    # in #1234.
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  #
  # Two suppression channels with different contracts:
  # - `// crap:ignore` (needs ignorable: true) = a JUSTIFIED structural
  #   twin, suppressed forever, with a one-line reason in the comment.
  # - `.crap-baseline.json` (via `check --baseline`) = LEGACY debt; the
  #   committed snapshot must only SHRINK: after each triage batch re-run
  #   `dart pub global run crap4dart check --save-baseline` and commit the
  #   only-down diff, or the snapshot rots and starts masking shifts.
  #
  # WINDOW (until severity flips to error): the gate never fails a build —
  # new (not-baselined) duplication only surfaces as a `[WARN]` line in
  # `check` output. Enforcement becomes hard exactly when the owner-side
  # escalation lands; from then on any finding outside the two channels
  # fails CI/pre-commit.
  duplication:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out
    sources: # cross-module scope from #487
      - flutter_app/lib
      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:
      # TUI screenshots, not goldens: amber/yellow text on the dark theme
      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for
      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.
      - 'test/integration/**'

# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo: 12.0 (re-measured whole-tree on
  # the merged-suite lcov, #1234 rework). The card's named offenders DID
  # move — readPasteboardImage 16.32 (split into fake-seam /
  # platform-dispatch helpers), the CC-12 trio (_handleTreeKey,
  # discoverTaskAgents, _rebuild) split into cohesive sub-dispatchers,
  # the four 0%-cov CC-3 methods covered by tests (frontmatter, video
  # endpoint, below-window ingest, provider picker), the named CC-9 tier
  # split, and _listModels (20 @ 0%) covered by the line-mode /models
  # test. But the FIRST real whole-tree measurement (the authoring box

  # Threshold stays at the measured max; the 12.00/9.00 tier is the next

  # then the threshold follows down to 8.0). Only down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
  # _listModels used to hit 20 with 0% coverage (line-mode-only output);
  # covered by test/cli/provider_models_line_mode_test.dart in #1234.

# ─── loc gate (issue #1234, gh-1232 migration) ─────────────────────────────
# The ≤2800-line file guard MOVED from scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_size +
# the ci.yml shell find-exec guards onto crap4dart's `loc` gate (0.11.0,
# maintainer-confirmed wc -l semantics). Enforced whole-tree on every merge

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right

# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the

gates:
  # Issue #1234: the whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was stage_size +
  # ci.yml shell find-exec, gh-1232). wc -l semantics, generated output
  # excluded — nothing exceeds 2800 today, so the shrink-only baseline
  # starts EMPTY of loc entries. Scope = the package sources [lib, bin]:

  # example/ are enforced by the companion config

  # the app package's own config covers flutter_app/lib.

    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - '**.g.dart'
      - '**.freezed.dart'
      - '**.mocks.dart'
      - 'vendor/**'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false} # follow-up card (issue #1234 §5). Known
    # FPs to exclude when enabling: the conditional-export IO entry points

    # importers live outside this repo's import graph) and shared pinned
    # data modules imported only from test/ (lib/src/cli/omp_reg_scenarios.dart,
    # issue #810). lib/fanet.dart was the one confirmed-dead hit — deleted
    # in #1234.

  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.

  # Two suppression channels with different contracts:
  # - `// crap:ignore` (needs ignorable: true) = a JUSTIFIED structural
  #   twin, suppressed forever, with a one-line reason in the comment.
  # - `.crap-baseline.json` (via `check --baseline`) = LEGACY debt; the
  #   committed snapshot must only SHRINK: after each triage batch re-run
  #   `dart pub global run crap4dart check --save-baseline` and commit the
  #   only-down diff, or the snapshot rots and starts masking shifts.
  #
  # WINDOW (until severity flips to error): the gate never fails a build —
  # new (not-baselined) duplication only surfaces as a `[WARN]` line in
  # `check` output. Enforcement becomes hard exactly when the owner-side
  # escalation lands; from then on any finding outside the two channels
  # fails CI/pre-commit.
  duplication:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out
    sources: # cross-module scope from #487

      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:

    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:

      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for
      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.
      - 'test/integration/**'

# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo: 12.0 (re-measured whole-tree on
  # the merged-suite lcov, #1234 rework). The card's named offenders DID
  # move — readPasteboardImage 16.32 (split into fake-seam /
  # platform-dispatch helpers), the CC-12 trio (_handleTreeKey,
  # discoverTaskAgents, _rebuild) split into cohesive sub-dispatchers,
  # the four 0%-cov CC-3 methods covered by tests (frontmatter, video
  # endpoint, below-window ingest, provider picker), the named CC-9 tier
  # split, and _listModels (20 @ 0%) covered by the line-mode /models
  # test. But the FIRST real whole-tree measurement (the authoring box
  # had no dart toolchain) shows the 12.0 → 8.0 repin is not earned yet:
  # 137 methods measure above 8.0 — 54 at exactly 12.00 (the CC-3 @ 0%
  # tier + fully-covered CC-12 dispatchers) and 83 at 9.00 (CC-9 @ 100%).
  # Threshold stays at the measured max; the 12.00/9.00 tier is the next
  # ladder card (cover the CC-3@0% half, split the CC-12 dispatchers,
  # then the threshold follows down to 8.0). Only down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
  # _listModels used to hit 20 with 0% coverage (line-mode-only output);
  # covered by test/cli/provider_models_line_mode_test.dart in #1234.

# ─── loc gate (issue #1234, gh-1232 migration) ─────────────────────────────
# The ≤2800-line file guard MOVED from scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_size +
# the ci.yml shell find-exec guards onto crap4dart's `loc` gate (0.11.0,
# maintainer-confirmed wc -l semantics). Enforced whole-tree on every merge
# validation via `crap4dart check --baseline` (CI quality-gates step) and
# staged files in the pre-commit hook — no staged-scoping escape, no
# hook-dependence, merge-bot merges included. max_lines only DOWN;
# app_localizations.dart is gen-l10n OUTPUT (no .g.dart suffix) — excluded,
# not baselined.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  # Issue #1234: the whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was stage_size +
  # ci.yml shell find-exec, gh-1232). wc -l semantics, generated output
  # excluded — nothing exceeds 2800 today, so the shrink-only baseline
  # starts EMPTY of loc entries. Scope = the package sources [lib, bin]:
  # 0.11.0 has NO per-gate sources override (gates.loc.sources is a
  # ConfigException — caught by CI on 019ede65), and the top-level
  # sources drive the CRAP census too, so they stay untouched. test/ and
  # example/ are enforced by the companion config
  # crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml (same loc gate, sources [test, example]);
  # the app package's own config covers flutter_app/lib.
  loc:
    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - '**.g.dart'
      - '**.freezed.dart'
      - '**.mocks.dart'
      - 'vendor/**'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false} # follow-up card (issue #1234 §5). Known
    # FPs to exclude when enabling: the conditional-export IO entry points
    # (lib/io.dart, lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart — public barrels whose
    # importers live outside this repo's import graph) and shared pinned
    # data modules imported only from test/ (lib/src/cli/omp_reg_scenarios.dart,
    # issue #810). lib/fanet.dart was the one confirmed-dead hit — deleted
    # in #1234.
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  #
  # Two suppression channels with different contracts:
  # - `// crap:ignore` (needs ignorable: true) = a JUSTIFIED structural
  #   twin, suppressed forever, with a one-line reason in the comment.
  # - `.crap-baseline.json` (via `check --baseline`) = LEGACY debt; the
  #   committed snapshot must only SHRINK: after each triage batch re-run
  #   `dart pub global run crap4dart check --save-baseline` and commit the
  #   only-down diff, or the snapshot rots and starts masking shifts.
  #
  # WINDOW (until severity flips to error): the gate never fails a build —
  # new (not-baselined) duplication only surfaces as a `[WARN]` line in
  # `check` output. Enforcement becomes hard exactly when the owner-side
  # escalation lands; from then on any finding outside the two channels
  # fails CI/pre-commit.
  duplication:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out
    sources: # cross-module scope from #487
      - flutter_app/lib
      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]

crap:
  enabled: true

  test_assertions: {enabled: false}

The upsert writes `auto_update: true` as a scalar line at top-level, validated with the real parser. Good.

Note: `_upsertConfigYaml` calls `loadYaml(edited)` WITHOUT try — if the edited yaml throws (e.g. user's file has a duplicate key that becomes invalid after insertion?), it throws unhandled. Pre-existing pattern though.

Now, `_writeAutoUpdateYaml` passes `validate: autoUpdateModeFromYaml` — the validate call receives `doc[segments.first]` = the parsed value (`true`/`false`/`'notify'`). `autoUpdateModeFromYaml(true)` → on ✓.

Interesting subtlety: yaml parsing of `auto_update: on` → yaml 1.1 would parse `on` as boolean true! The yaml package (dart) is yaml 1.2-ish: `on` is parsed as STRING 'on' in dart's yaml package (dart yaml follows YAML 1.1 partially... Actually dart `yaml` package treats `on`/`off`/`yes`/`no` as strings — YAML 1.2 core schema has no yes/no/on/off booleans. dart yaml: booleans are true/false/True/False/TRUE/FALSE only. So `auto_update: on` → string 'on' → autoUpdateModeFromYaml throws ConfigException → strict error message. Boot would FAIL on `auto_update: on`. The error message names the legal values — acceptable strict behavior, matches "strict like every scalar". The docs/help say `auto_update: notify|true|false` — consistent. OK.

# Changelog

## 1.0.508


- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake

  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an

# Changelog

## 1.0.508


- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate

CHANGELOG is maintained by release chores, not feature PRs — feature PR #1263 didn't touch it (only release chores). So no CHANGELOG expectation. ✓

Now finalize the findings list. Let me consolidate:

### BLOCKING

**B1. `/update` restart silently abandons the active session for plain `fa` launches** (bin/fah_runapp.dart `_runSlashUpdate` / `updateCommand` closure — line in diff). The successor is spawned with the ORIGINAL argv; without an explicit `--session` on the command line the successor boots a NEW empty session (`_initializeSession` → `_createSession()`), so the "session resumes with full history" AC (and the slash-menu text "restart fa (same session)") is not delivered for the default launch style. The transcript survives on disk but the user is dropped into a fresh session with no pointer to the old one. Fix: bind the live session id at spawn time (the closure needs a late-bound session-id getter, since `updateCommand` is built before the session boots) and append `--session <id>` when the running session was implicitly created.

Line to anchor: bin/fah_runapp.dart — the `updateCommand: () => _runSlashUpdate(...)` lines (~1409-1417 in new file; in diff hunk `@@ -1351,6 +1406,18`). I need a line number present in the diff: the diff shows `updateCommand: () => _runSlashUpdate(` added at new-file line ~1412. Let me get exact line numbers in the new file for anchoring. Also `_runSlashUpdate` at 1677+. And the boot hook lines 246-296.

Actually — wait. I should double-check this claim once more. Is there any chance the TUI session boot sets `--session`-like state that the successor picks up? E.g. a "most recent session" resume heuristic? `_initializeSession` → no name → `_createSession()`. Definitive. BLOCKING confirmed.

**B2. Unbounded auto-update respawn loop when the swap/activation doesn't advance the running version** (bin/self_manage.dart applyUpdate pubGlobal branch + no loop guard in the boot hook).
- pub-global + `auto_update: on` + pub.dev lagging GitHub (a state the code itself anticipates and comments on): `dart pub global activate` exits 0 without changing the running snapshot version → log "fa update applied vX -> vY" (false) → spawn successor → successor is still vX → fetches GitHub → newer → activate → spawn → … forever. Each cycle spawns a process and hits GitHub + pub.dev.
- binary installs with a mis-tagged release (binary's version.txt/packageVersion < tag) loop the same way, re-downloading the whole archive on every boot.
Fix suggestions: after activation, re-read the activated version (`dart pub global list`) and refuse to restart when it didn't advance (return a distinct outcome); for binary, verify the staged bundle's version.txt > current before swapping, and/or persist a last-attempted tag marker in ~/.fah as a circuit breaker.

Anchor: the `log('fa update applied: v$currentVersion -> v$latest');` line in the pubGlobal branch of applyUpdate.

Severity check: requires opt-in `auto_update: on` — but that's the flag this PR ships; the pub-lag window is normal operation. Unbounded loop = broken behavior → BLOCKING.

### IMPORTANT

**I1. The default `notify` check adds a network round-trip (up to 3 stall) to every boot, including headless/CI runs.** `fetchLatestTag().timeout(3s)` runs before any session work on every `fa` invocation (default mode). On air-gapped/firewalled hosts every run stalls ~3 s; each run also contacts GitHub (privacy/telemetry-adjacent surprise for a "no telemetry" project). Suggest skipping the check for headless runs (`headlessPrompt != null`) or running it post-boot/async; the timeout client leak compounds it.

Anchor: the `fetchLatestTag().timeout(` lines in fah_runapp.dart boot hook.

**I2. Boot hook prints "auto update failed (unsupportedPlatform) — continuing" on Windows after a SUCCESSFUL swap.** On Windows `applyUpdate` returns `unsupportedPlatform` after the binary was already swapped and the engine printed "updated to vX — restart fa to use it." — the boot hook's `case _:` then prints "auto update failed (unsupportedPlatform)" — contradicting the engine's success message. The explicit `case ApplyUpdateOutcome.unsupportedPlatform: break;` exists in `_runSlashUpdate` but not in the boot hook's inner switch.

Anchor: the `case _:` block in the boot hook switch (fah_runapp.dart).

**I3. `applyUpdate` pub-global branch has zero test coverage** — the new autonomous pub-global path (activate → log → restart via spawnSuccessor/`_whichFa`) is untested (the applyUpdate outcome matrix covers binary only), and it's exactly where B2 lives.

Anchor: self_manage_test.dart applyUpdate group — hmm, inline comments must anchor to diff lines. The applyUpdate group start `group('applyUpdate', () {` is an added line ✓.

### SUGGESTIONS

**S1. `fetchLatestTag().timeout(3s, onTimeout: () => null)` abandons the in-flight HTTP request and leaks its client** — the `.timeout` wrapper returns while the underlying request keeps its socket open (fetchLatestTag's `finally` only runs when the original future completes). Consider a client with a proper connection timeout or cancel the request on timeout.

**S2. `/update` prints nothing for `unsupportedPlatform` on platforms with no prebuilt archive** (`_archiveName()` → null): the silent `break` assumes "the engine already printed the restart prompt after the swap", but the no-archive path swaps nothing and prints nothing — user gets zero feedback. (Windows swap path does print.) One writeln would fix.

**S3. `_extractZip`/tar extraction has no zip-slip hardening** — pre-existing, but the PR turns it into an autonomous boot-time path; entry names (`../`) are only mitigated by the provenance gate. Defense-in-depth: reject entries escaping tmpDir.

**S4. `applyUpdate`'s catch-all reports every unexpected failure as `downloadFailed`** — a mid-swap file error is indistinguishable from a network failure in the one-line boot warning; a distinct outcome (or rethrow-with-context) would make the fa.log line actionable.

Maybe also: `_warn` to stderr in `_restartAfterUpdate` mid-TUI — minor, skip.

**S5?** `_dropTopLevelBlock('auto_update')` matches the first line starting with `auto_update:` anywhere — a block-scalar containing that text would be mangled (pre-existing pattern via 'agent'); skip or fold into a note? I'll skip — pre-existing pattern, low value.

CHANGELOG is maintained by release chores, not feature PRs — feature PR #1263 didn't touch it (only release chores). So no CHANGELOG expectation. ✓

Now finalize the findings list. Let me consolidate:

### BLOCKING

**B1. `/update` restart silently abandons the active session for plain `fa` launches** (bin/fah_runapp.dart `_runSlashUpdate` / `updateCommand` closure — line in diff). The successor is spawned with the ORIGINAL argv; without an explicit `--session` on the command line the successor boots a NEW empty session (`_initializeSession` → `_createSession()`), so the "session resumes with full history" AC (and the slash-menu text "restart fa (same session)") is not delivered for the default launch style. The transcript survives on disk but the user is dropped into a fresh session with no pointer to the old one. Fix: bind the live session id at spawn time (the closure needs a late-bound session-id getter, since `updateCommand` is built before the session boots) and append `--session <id>` when the running session was implicitly created.

Line to anchor: bin/fah_runapp.dart — the `updateCommand: () => _runSlashUpdate(...)` lines (~1409-1417 in new file; in diff hunk `@@ -1351,6 +1406,18`). I need a line number present in the diff: the diff shows `updateCommand: () => _runSlashUpdate(` added at new-file line ~1412. Let me get exact line numbers in the new file for anchoring. Also `_runSlashUpdate` at 1677+. And the boot hook lines 246-296.

Actually — wait. I should double-check this claim once more. Is there any chance the TUI session boot sets `--session`-like state that the successor picks up? E.g. a "most recent session" resume heuristic? `_initializeSession` → no name → `_createSession()`. Definitive. BLOCKING confirmed.

**B2. Unbounded auto-update respawn loop when the swap/activation doesn't advance the running version** (bin/self_manage.dart applyUpdate pubGlobal branch + no loop guard in the boot hook).
- pub-global + `auto_update: on` + pub.dev lagging GitHub (a state the code itself anticipates and comments on): `dart pub global activate` exits 0 without changing the running snapshot version → log "fa update applied vX -> vY" (false) → spawn successor → successor is still vX → fetches GitHub → newer → activate → spawn → … forever. Each cycle spawns a process and hits GitHub + pub.dev.
- binary installs with a mis-tagged release (binary's version.txt/packageVersion < tag) loop the same way, re-downloading the whole archive on every boot.
Fix suggestions: after activation, re-read the activated version (`dart pub global list`) and refuse to restart when it didn't advance (return a distinct outcome); for binary, verify the staged bundle's version.txt > current before swapping, and/or persist a last-attempted tag marker in ~/.fah as a circuit breaker.

Anchor: the `log('fa update applied: v$currentVersion -> v$latest');` line in the pubGlobal branch of applyUpdate.

Severity check: requires opt-in `auto_update: on` — but that's the flag this PR ships; the pub-lag window is normal operation. Unbounded loop = broken behavior → BLOCKING.

### IMPORTANT

**I1. The default `notify` check adds a network round-trip (up to 3 stall) to every boot, including headless/CI runs.** `fetchLatestTag().timeout(3s)` runs before any session work on every `fa` invocation (default mode). On air-gapped/firewalled hosts every run stalls ~3 s; each run also contacts GitHub (privacy/telemetry-adjacent surprise for a "no telemetry" project). Suggest skipping the check for headless runs (`headlessPrompt != null`) or running it post-boot/async; the timeout client leak compounds it.

Anchor: the `fetchLatestTag().timeout(` lines in fah_runapp.dart boot hook.

**I2. Boot hook prints "auto update failed (unsupportedPlatform) — continuing" on Windows after a SUCCESSFUL swap.** On Windows `applyUpdate` returns `unsupportedPlatform` after the binary was already swapped and the engine printed "updated to vX — restart fa to use it." — the boot hook's `case _:` then prints "auto update failed (unsupportedPlatform)" — contradicting the engine's success message. The explicit `case ApplyUpdateOutcome.unsupportedPlatform: break;` exists in `_runSlashUpdate` but not in the boot hook's inner switch.

Anchor: the `case _:` block in the boot hook switch (fah_runapp.dart).

**I3. `applyUpdate` pub-global branch has zero test coverage** — the new autonomous pub-global path (activate → log → restart via spawnSuccessor/`_whichFa`) is untested (the applyUpdate outcome matrix covers binary only), and it's exactly where B2 lives.

# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.

# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo: 12.0 (re-measured whole-tree on
  # the merged-suite lcov, #1234 rework). The card's named offenders DID
  # move — readPasteboardImage 16.32 (split into fake-seam /
  # platform-dispatch helpers), the CC-12 trio (_handleTreeKey,
  # discoverTaskAgents, _rebuild) split into cohesive sub-dispatchers,
  # the four 0%-cov CC-3 methods covered by tests (frontmatter, video
  # endpoint, below-window ingest, provider picker), the named CC-9 tier
  # split, and _listModels (20 @ 0%) covered by the line-mode /models
  # test. But the FIRST real whole-tree measurement (the authoring box
  # had no dart toolchain) shows the 12.0 → 8.0 repin is not earned yet:
  # 137 methods measure above 8.0 — 54 at exactly 12.00 (the CC-3 @ 0%
  # tier + fully-covered CC-12 dispatchers) and 83 at 9.00 (CC-9 @ 100%).
  # Threshold stays at the measured max; the 12.00/9.00 tier is the next
  # ladder card (cover the CC-3@0% half, split the CC-12 dispatchers,
  # then the threshold follows down to 8.0). Only down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
  # _listModels used to hit 20 with 0% coverage (line-mode-only output);
  # covered by test/cli/provider_models_line_mode_test.dart in #1234.

# ─── loc gate (issue #1234, gh-1232 migration) ─────────────────────────────
# The ≤2800-line file guard MOVED from scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_size +
# the ci.yml shell find-exec guards onto crap4dart's `loc` gate (0.11.0,
# maintainer-confirmed wc -l semantics). Enforced whole-tree on every merge
# validation via `crap4dart check --baseline` (CI quality-gates step) and
# staged files in the pre-commit hook — no staged-scoping escape, no
# hook-dependence, merge-bot merges included. max_lines only DOWN;
# app_localizations.dart is gen-l10n OUTPUT (no .g.dart suffix) — excluded,
# not baselined.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  # Issue #1234: the whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was stage_size +
  # ci.yml shell find-exec, gh-1232). wc -l semantics, generated output
  # excluded — nothing exceeds 2800 today, so the shrink-only baseline
  # starts EMPTY of loc entries. Scope = the package sources [lib, bin]:
  # 0.11.0 has NO per-gate sources override (gates.loc.sources is a
  # ConfigException — caught by CI on 019ede65), and the top-level
  # sources drive the CRAP census too, so they stay untouched. test/ and
  # example/ are enforced by the companion config
  # crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml (same loc gate, sources [test, example]);
  # the app package's own config covers flutter_app/lib.
  loc:
    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - '**.g.dart'
      - '**.freezed.dart'
      - '**.mocks.dart'
      - 'vendor/**'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false} # follow-up card (issue #1234 §5). Known
    # FPs to exclude when enabling: the conditional-export IO entry points

    # importers live outside this repo's import graph) and shared pinned
    # data modules imported only from test/ (lib/src/cli/omp_reg_scenarios.dart,

  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid

  #

  # - `// crap:ignore` (needs ignorable: true) = a JUSTIFIED structural
